limitations: The 32/64 pair is uniform; the 128 run includes one rejected parent interval and two accepted half intervals. No uniform three-level convergence study is claimed.

All positions and saved velocities are compared without registration or interpolation. Saved backward-Euler velocities average different preceding intervals; common 2 ms secants are separate diagnostics.

Geometric angles and contact energies are producer observations bound to report bytes; held force vectors are the negative saved analytic sewing gradient on vertex 2. No physical forces or path proofs are recomputed.
A common nonzero initial contact potential causes initial relaxation. All controls, targets, rest geometry, source helpers, physical duration and solver tolerances are identical across current runs.

Window state statistics include both boundary states. Window work includes only accepted intervals with start boundary < end fraction <= end boundary. Ranges, net changes and total variation are distinct.
Own-grid peaks can change because finer samples resolve peaks. Common-grid peaks and common-window secants are reported separately. This does not bound unsampled extrema.

Discrete parameter work depends on the resolved path and partition even under identical continuous control inputs. The signed energy remainder is not calibrated dissipation or continuous actuator work.
Fold release preserves the held scalar seam, contact and passive cloth forces. Null actuator angles do not indicate zero geometric angles; no all-controls-free or settled tail exists.
Each run follows a different piecewise affine path. Independent path/candidate coverage is a separate artifact; stored successful reports checked here are not independently reproduced proofs.
Only two scalar seam samples, one held and one pending. No continuous spatial seam, garment construction, material calibration, stability, convergence order or application acceptance follows.
Callback files are private research artifacts, not supervised crash-safe captured execution. Resource-cap failure remains retained and is not silently converted to a successful run.
